Title: Hyperliquid Strategies Ramps Up Buyback Plan to $100M After Stock Sell-Off
Author: Editorial Staff   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:24 PM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T21:24:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
HYPE treasury firm Hyperliquid Strategies Inc (NASDAQ: $PURR), has increased its stock repurchase program to $100 million from $30 million and pushed the program's end date to October 31, 2027.
The Nasdaq-listed company announced the change last Friday after the market close. Approximately $72 million remains available under the larger authorization, which implies about $28 million has been used so far. The program previously ran through Dec. 5, 2026.
Hyperliquid Strategies said the increase reflects its board's confidence in the company's long-term capital strategy and gives it room to buy back shares as part of its treasury management. It can repurchase shares on the open market, in privately negotiated deals or by other methods allowed under federal securities laws. Management decides the timing and size of purchases based on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements. The company said there is no guarantee how many shares it will buy and that it can extend, suspend or end the program at any time.
Cardano Founder Hoskinson Says Midnight Will Surpass Zcash, Urges Gemini to List ADA
Stacks Founder Warns Bitcoin Security Breach Could Hit Entire Crypto Market
Coinbase Targets Banks As Institutional Crypto Adoption Grows
60 Percent of Community Banks See Stablecoins as a Threat to Deposits, Lending
Crypto Heavyweights Back OKX at $25B Valuation
The expansion follows a sharp drop in the stock. PURR traded near $8.80 on Friday, about 33% below its Oct. 5 high of $13.05. HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid (CRYPTO: $HYPE) blockchain, traded around $77, while bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) held mostly between $80,000 and $87,000 in October.
The company acknowledged that its share price is closely tied to HYPE, listing the token's price volatility among its main risks. Hyperliquid Strategies describes itself as the largest treasury vehicle focused on HYPE, offering U.S. and institutional investors a way to hold the token while earning returns through staking, yield strategies and ecosystem participation.
Shares of Hyperliquid Strategies (NASDAQ: PURR) are currently trading at $9.07, down from a 52 week high of $14.76.

Title: Can Hyperliquid (HYPE) Get Back to $90 by the End of 2026?
Author: Sam Daodu   Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:20 AM GMT+2 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-24T23:20:04+00:00
=== BODY ===
HYPE trades around $76, needing a 19.2% gain to reach $90, while sitting 22.9% below its September peak.
HYPE's fully diluted valuation hits $72 billion today, rising to $86 billion at $90, as 77% of total supply remains out of circulation.
Hyperliquid Strategies expanded its stock buyback to $100 million, which could indirectly ease selling pressure on HYPE tokens.
It sounds nuts, but SoFi is giving new Active Invest users up to $1,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started. See for yourself (Sponsor)
Hyperliquid (CRYPTO:HYPE) needs to gain 19.2% to climb back to the significant milestone of $90, a target many holders have set between its price and its record high of $98. The Hyperliquid price stands at approximately $76 as of October 24, 2026.
HYPE has decreased by 3% in the last 24 hours, 5.2% over the past week, and 17.1% over the last 30 days. This performance puts it about 22.9% below its peak on September 23.
In the past day, HYPE has traded between $75 and $79. On October 23, Hyperliquid Strategies, a public company that holds HYPE as its main treasury asset, expanded its stock buyback program, drawing renewed attention to the token.
If HYPE reaches $90, its market capitalization would soar to around $20 billion. This figure is calculated by multiplying the token price by the total number of tokens in circulation. With 222.4 million HYPE available, a $90 price would mark a significant increase from its current market cap of about $16.8 billion, which places it 11th among cryptocurrencies.
However, there is a concern regarding supply dilution. HYPE's total supply is 955.3 million, with a hard cap of 1 billion. This means about 77% of the tokens created are yet to be in circulation.
SoFi Active Invest is offering a limited-time promotion. Open an account, fund it with $50 or more, and you could receive up to $1,000 in complimentary stock for Active Invest accounts. See for yourself by clicking here now. (Sponsor)
With all 955.3 million tokens counted, HYPE's fully diluted valuation already reaches $72 billion and would rise to approximately $86 billion at a $90 price. To reach that price, HYPE would need new investment, making a $90 target in December harder than it was during the September run-up.
Still, HYPE shows strength over the longer term, up 107.1% over the past 200 days and 90.1% year-over-year, while Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) has dropped 27.4% in the same timeframe. Bitcoin currently trades at $80,483, down 4.4% over the past month. HYPE's larger decline than Bitcoin's could indicate that a weak Bitcoin market in November and December would make it harder for HYPE to achieve the necessary 19.2% increase.
Hyperliquid operates a decentralized exchange that primarily offers perpetual futures tracking the price of various coins without expiry dates. The platform's Assistance Fund collects trading fees and uses them to buy HYPE tokens on the open market, so a busier trading environment can lead to more automatic HYPE purchases.
Since early October, additional revenue from Hyperliquid's USDC reserves has provided another source of capital for buying HYPE. Users keep about $8.2 billion deposited on the platform—known as total value locked—and HYPE has seen about $767 million in trading volume over the last 24 hours.
Despite these buybacks, HYPE has still lost value, dropping 17.1% over the past month as sellers and unlocked tokens have outpaced the Assistance Fund's purchases since the September peak.
Hyperliquid Strategies (NASDAQ:PURR), a digital asset treasury company that considers HYPE its core asset, raised its stock repurchase program to $100 million on October 23.
While this buyback focuses on the company's stock rather than HYPE tokens directly, it can still indirectly benefit HYPE. When a company buys back its own shares, it has less incentive to sell HYPE to prop up its stock price, which could ease selling pressure on the token.
A webcast scheduled for November 5 will provide updates for the quarter ended September 30. Any announcements regarding HYPE holdings or new token purchases could influence market sentiment.
HYPE seems unlikely to reach $90 by year-end, given the steep 19.2% climb, growing unlocked supply, and a 30-day downtrend. For HYPE to have a chance, it must first break $79, the top of its latest 24-hour range and about 4.2% higher. Additionally, the November 5 webcast needs to show Hyperliquid Strategies adding HYPE, and platform trading must pick up so the Assistance Fund's purchases can outpace new supply.
If HYPE continues to trade below $79 after the November 5 webcast, reaching $90 will likely be postponed until 2027. Conversely, if it closes above $79 before then, the $90 target could become possible in December.

Title: TRON (TRX) and Hyperliquid (HYPE) Are About 23% Below Their Record Highs. Solana Is 66% Below. Which Gets Back First?
Author: Sam Daodu   Sun, October 25, 2026 at 9:00 PM GMT+1 6 min read
Published: 2026-10-25T20:00:30+00:00
=== BODY ===
HYPE needs only a 28% rally to reclaim its all-time high set just a month ago, while SOL requires a massive 190% gain from its current price.
Hyperliquid directs 99% of protocol fees to HYPE buybacks and burns, with the ecosystem generating about $945 million in value over the past year.
Solana's Alpenglow upgrade, considered the protocol's most significant change ever, launched October 21 but SOL has since fallen about 5.5%.
It sounds nuts, but SoFi is giving new Active Invest users up to $1,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started. See for yourself (Sponsor)
TRON (CRYPTO:TRX) and Hyperliquid (CRYPTO:HYPE) are both trading within 24% of their all-time highs, while Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) trades 65.6% below its peak value. As of October 25, 2026, TRX is priced at about $0.33, just 23.7% below its record high of $0.43, set on December 3, 2024. Meanwhile, HYPE is trading at about $76, which is 21.9% below its all-time high of $98 from September 23.
In contrast, SOL trades at about $101, significantly down from its peak of $293 on January 19, 2025. Since late September, SOL has fluctuated between a high of $125 on September 27 and a low of $99 on October 24, and it has declined 47.2% over the past year.
So, which of these three coins is most likely to reach a new all-time high first?
An all-time high represents the highest price a cryptocurrency has ever achieved. A recovery requires a larger percentage gain than the prior drop because the rebound starts from a lower price. For example, a coin that falls 23.7% will need to gain 31.1% from its reduced price to regain its peak.
SoFi Active Invest is offering a limited-time promotion. Open an account, fund it with $50 or more, and you could receive up to $1,000 in complimentary stock for Active Invest accounts. See for yourself by clicking here now. (Sponsor)
HYPE requires the smallest increase at 28.1%, with TRX close behind at 31.1%. In stark contrast, SOL would need a massive 190.4% rally to reclaim its former glory. However, momentum varies widely among these coins. Over the last 30 days, TRX has slipped only 2.4%, while HYPE has dropped 18.1% and SOL has fallen 16.5%.
TRON operates a blockchain designed for low-cost transactions, primarily driven by the high volume of USDT, Tether's dollar-pegged stablecoin. Users pay network fees in TRX, leading to consistent demand for the token due to heavy stablecoin traffic.
A Nansen report released on October 22 highlighted TRON's strong position in stablecoin settlement volume for the third quarter and the introduction of the first TRX exchange-traded fund, which lets investors hold TRX through brokerage accounts.
Despite this strong usage, TRX has shown limited price movement, with only a 2.4% decline over the past month. This suggests a trading pattern within a narrow range, indicating that a significant climb to regain 31.1% might require sustained positive revenue growth.
Hyperliquid operates a decentralized exchange focused on perpetual futures—contracts that track asset prices without expiration. The protocol allocates trading fees to an Assistance Fund, which buys HYPE tokens from the market. Hyperliquid Strategies (NASDAQ:PURR) says 99% of protocol fees go towards HYPE buybacks and token burns. In its August 27 report, the Hyperliquid ecosystem generated about $945 million in value over the past year.
Furthermore, Hyperliquid Strategies said Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) would transfer about 90% of the reserve yield on $5.5 billion of USDC to the protocol, starting October 3. On October 23, the treasury company also increased its stock buyback program to $100 million, although this targets PURR shares rather than HYPE. Nevertheless, HYPE faces higher momentum risks, having dropped 18.1% in the last month.
The Alpenglow upgrade aims to enhance Solana's consensus process, which validates transactions. The Solana Foundation considers it the most significant change to the Solana protocol, with the first phase launching on October 21. This upgrade reportedly reduces transaction finality to a fraction of a second. However, SOL's price closed at $107 on the day of the upgrade and has since fallen about 5.5% to $101.
In the long run, decentralized finance applications and stablecoins may increase demand for SOL. That said, SOL's most active trading day in the past month was October 8, when it fell 5.7% from $116 to $110.
In our estimation, HYPE has the best shot at reaching a new all-time high first. It needs the smallest rally at 28.1%; it set its record only a month ago, and ongoing buybacks support the token. TRX follows closely at 31.1% but moves more slowly, which could delay its climb back to $0.43 until HYPE surpasses $98. Solana appears the least likely to recover quickly, as it must first overcome $125, about 23.7% higher.
However, this prediction comes with risks. If Hyperliquid's fee revenue declines, the Assistance Fund may buy fewer tokens, pushing HYPE lower than TRX. If HYPE exceeds $98 before TRX reaches $0.43, our analysis stands. Yet, if SOL dips below its $99 low from October 24, it would face an even steeper challenge in reclaiming its previous heights.
